title: WPSS/3740/2018 of SUDHIR RANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPSS No. 3740 of 2018
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. K.K. Tiwari, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. P.C. Bisht and Ms. Anjali Bhargava, Addl.
C.S.C. with Mr. N.P. Sah and Mr. Sushil Vasistha,
Standing Counsel for the State.
 By means of present petition, petitioner has
sought following relief:
(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
certiorari quashing the impugned order dated
19.09.2018 issued by respondent no.3.
(ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing and commanding the
respondents to count the services rendered by the
petitioner in the department of Commercial Tax
for the purpose of computation of probation
period and thereafter the petitioner be promoted
to the post of Senior Assistant w.e.f. 31.03.2011
the day when other similarly situated candidates
appointed through the same selection process in
which the petitioner participated.
(iii)Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding and directing the
respondent no.2 to promote the petitioner to the
post of Chief Assistant w.e.f. 09.10.2015
alongwith all consequential benefits which was
done in the case of similarly situated persons.
Brief facts of the case are that vide G.O. dated
24.12.2005, the Govind Ballabh Pant University of
Agriculture and Technology, Pant Nagar was
authorized to conduct a written examination for the
post of Junior Assistants in various Department. The
District Magistrates of all the Districts were appointed
as Nodal Officer for the aforesaid purpose. In District
Dehradun 08 posts of Junior Assistants were vacant
in the office of Transport Commissioner, Uttarakhand,
Dehradun. An advertisement for such vacancies was
issued in various newspapers on 30.06.2006 for which
the petitioner also applied. A written examination and
typing test was conducted, whereafter the respondent
no.4 recommended names of six candidates. On
11.12.2008, appointment orders too all six selected
candidates were issued. Pursuant to which, four
candidates joined the services on 12.12.2018 and two
candidates gave their joining on 15.12.2008 &
03.01.2019. Thereafter, on the basis of marks
obtained and the post advertised, recommendation

was made to provisionally appoint two more
candidates in the Department. Pursuant to the said
recommendation, the petitioner was issued an
appointment letter on 18.06.2009. In compliance of
the same, the petitioner joined his services as Junior
Assistant in the Department.
 The grievance of the petitioner is that the Junior
Assistant, who were appointed in pursuant to the
same selection process but appointed prior to the
petitioner were promoted to the post of Senior
Assistant vide order dated 31.03.2011 only after
completion of two and three years of their service
whereas the petitioner has been discriminated on
account of delayed appointment.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit
that as per Rules, 2011 the next promotional post of
Senior Assistant is Chief Assistant and the minimum
qualifying service for being promoted to the post of
Chief Assistant is three years on the post of Senior
Assistant and total service must be eleven years on
the subordinate post. He would further submit that
the Junior Assistant appointed prior to the petitioner
though selected in the same selection process were
promoted to the post of Chief Assistant after giving
relaxation in service condition as per the relaxation
rules. He would further submit that before the
petitioner could be promoted to the post of Senior
Assistants, new Rules of 2011 were enacted which
changed the qualifying service for promotion to the
higher posts. He would further submit that the
petitioner ought to have been promoted on the post of
Senior Assistant, when the other similarly situated
persons were promoted, but due to the enactment of
Rules, 2011 the petitioner was not promoted. Feeling
aggrieved, the petitioner filed a claim petition before
the Uttarakhand Public Service Tribunal, which was
decided vide order dated 23.06.2018 directing the
respondent no.3 to decide the representation of the
petitioner by a reasoned and speaking order in
accordance with law within a period of four weeks but
the respondent no.3 has not passed any order on the
petitionerís representation. Thereafter, the petitioner
filed a contempt petition before the Public Service
Tribunal. The said contempt petition was disposed of
with the direction that the authority concerned shall
comply with the earlier order passed by it within three

weeks. Thereafter, respondent no.3 vide order dated
20.09.2018 decided the representation of the
petitioner, whereby his claim has been rejected.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material available on record.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit
that it is settled principle of law that persons of similar
kind cannot be differentiated. He would further
submit that it will amount to gross discrimination if
the case of the petitioner is not considered at par with
the other similarly situate persons.
 Per contra, learned Government pleader would
submit that by the above named six employees were
promoted to the post of Chief Assistant by granting
one time relaxation in terms of Rules 2015. He would
further submit that as per the provisions contained in
the Rules those senior clerks will be eligible for
promotion as Chief Assistant who has completed 3
years service on the first day of the recruitment year
and must have completed ten years service on the
subordinate posts on the basis of seniority. He would
further submit that neither the petitioner has
completed three years of service as Senior Assistant
nor has he competed ten years of service on the
subordinate posts, when above referred six employees
were promoted, therefore, he is not entitled for
promotion as Chief Assistant. He would further
submit that the petitioner has already been granted
relaxation in qualifying services which is admissible
only once in the entire service tenure.
 To this, learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that on the basis of one advertisement, the
petitioner applied and participated in the written test
and thereafter six candidates were issued appointment
letters on 11.12.2008, while the petitioner and one
another were issued appointment letters on
15.12.2008 & 03.01.2009 belatedly. He would further
submit that a group of person in the same selection
cannot be treated as a class separate from the rest for
any preferential or beneficial treatment and it must be
based on objective consideration on a valid
classification.
Perusal of the record would reveal that similarly
situated persons have been given benefits of
promotion whereas the petitioner has been
discriminated from the others. The act of the

respondent is totally illegal and violative of Article 14
& 16 of the Constitution of India. Perusal of the record
would further reveal that the action of the respondent
in non considering the case of petitioner vis-‡-vis the
other similar situate candidates is wholly illegal,
arbitrary and discriminatory and, accordingly, cannot
be sustained in law.
 In the result, the impugned order dated
20.09.2020 is hereby quashed. Writ petition is
allowed. Respondent/Competent Authority is directed
to consider the case of the petitioner for promotion as
per his seniority and if he is found suitable, the
respondents shall promote him immediately from the
date, when the similar situate persons were given
promotion. Said exercise be completed within a period
of three months from the date of production of
certified copy of this order.
 Pending applications stand disposed of.
 No order as to costs.
